step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture diagram illustrates Addictive's real-time analytics and predictive ML platform for mobile ad revenue optimization. 1. Streaming events (~30,000 events/sec) are ingested into a Kafka cluster (ThirdParty). 2. An EKS cluster running Kafka Streams processes the incoming streams, computing real-time aggregation counters sent to RDS and dumping raw event data lake material (~400 GB/day, ~120 TB total) into S3. 3. S3 data is processed by a second EKS cluster running hundreds of isolated Spark ML jobs on Spot instances per customer. 4. Spark ML outputs aggregated prediction metrics to RDS and raw per-user prediction data to RedShift. 5. A React-based Client Dashboard calls a Go API service hosted on a third EKS cluster, which queries RDS for fast aggregated metrics and RedShift for raw prediction data.

graph.name: Addictive Predictive Analytics and ML Platform
graph.notes: System processes ~30k events/sec, adding 400 GB daily to a 120 TB S3 data lake. Uses EKS with Spot instances running hundreds of isolated Spark clusters for resilient, cost-effective ML model processing.

nodes.name: Kafka

nodes.name: EKS (Kafka Streams)
nodes.notes: Managed Kubernetes cluster running Kafka Streams applications for real-time aggregation and S3 raw ingestion.

nodes.name: S3
nodes.notes: S3 Data Lake storing raw user activity data (~400 GB added daily, managing ~120 TB total).

nodes.name: EKS (Spark)
nodes.notes: Managed Kubernetes cluster spawning hundreds of isolated Spark clusters on EC2 Spot instances for customer ML jobs.

nodes.name: RDS
nodes.notes: Relational database optimized for fast access to real-time aggregations and forecasting metrics.

nodes.name: Redshift
nodes.notes: Data warehouse storing raw per-user prediction outputs for flexible querying.

nodes.name: EKS (API)
nodes.notes: Managed Kubernetes cluster running backend API endpoints written in Go.

nodes.name: Client Dashboard
nodes.notes: React Web Application dashboard displaying revenue per user forecasts to customers.
